law: source/phase_law.h (per-cell arithmetic), source/phase_law_host.hpp (vapor knots, eps0), source/janaf_data.h (transcribed JANAF rows)

tags.measured: value taken from a primary measurement report
tags.recommended: critically evaluated or recommended value of a compilation, inside the range the source covers
tags.recommended_extrapolated_by_source: recommended value that the source itself states is extrapolated
tags.model_derived: value obtained by a stated model, continuation or choice in this law; not a source value

mills2004.cite: K. C. Mills, Y. Su, Z. Li, R. F. Brooks, Equations for the calculation of the thermo-physical properties of stainless steel, ISIJ International 44 (2004) 1661-1668
mills2004.note: derived from K. C. Mills, Recommended Values of Thermophysical Properties for Selected Commercial Alloys (Woodhead 2002), cited there as Ref. 7; the 2002 book itself was not accessed

hochu1977.cite: C. Y. Ho, T. K. Chu, Electrical resistivity and thermal conductivity of nine selected AISI stainless steels, CINDAS Report 45 (1977), DTIC ADA129160, Table 2 (AISI 304)
hochu1977.uncertainty: of the order of 5% below melting, 15% at or above melting; values above 1500 K extrapolated by the source (printed p. 4 and table footnotes)

nippon2020.cite: Nippon Steel Corporation, Stainless Steel Shapes, catalog S006en_02_202004, page 10 (TP 304 melting range 1399-1454 C)

janaf.cite: M. W. Chase Jr., NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, 4th ed., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data Monograph 9 (1998); tables Fe-006 Fe(l), Fe-008 Fe(g), Cr-003 Cr(l), Cr-005 Cr(g), Ni-003 Ni(l), Ni-005 Ni(g); cross-check tables Fe-007, Cr-004, Ni-004
janaf.uncertainty: per-table uncertainty statements are in the JANAF table texts (not the .txt files) and were not transcribed; cross-checks below bound the vapor law against an independent fit

alcock1984.cite: C. B. Alcock, V. P. Itkin, M. K. Horrigan, Vapour pressure equations for the metallic elements: 298-2500 K, Canadian Metallurgical Quarterly 23 (1984) 309
alcock1984.form: log10(p/atm) = A + B/T + C log10 T + D T/1000 (the D term multiplies T/1000; checked by solid/liquid continuity at the melting point for Fe and Sc)
alcock1984.stated_accuracy: 5% or better, for p in 1e-15..1e-3 atm
alcock1984.use: cross-check only (Fe and Ni liquid; Cr solid)

anisimov1968.cite: S. I. Anisimov, Vaporization of metal absorbing laser radiation, Sov. Phys. JETP 27 (1968) 182
anisimov1968.use: recondensation fraction of a sonic Knudsen layer (about 18% of the emitted flux returns)

sjostrom2023.cite: T. Sjostrom, Equation of state for 304L stainless steel, LA-UR-22-31200, doi 10.1063/12.0020364
sjostrom2023.use: critical point 9500 K, 0.615 GPa, 1.1 g/cm3 (domain-limit justification only)

mattsson2004.cite: T. R. Mattsson, M. P. Desjarlais, Equation of state and electrical conductivity of stainless steel, SAND2004-5253
mattsson2004.use: critical point 10000 K at 2 g/cc (SESAME 4272 about 2000 K lower) (domain-limit justification only)

bennett2023.cite: N. Bennett et al., Electrode plasma formation and melt in Z-pinch accelerators, Phys. Rev. Accel. Beams 26, 040401 (2023), Eq. (1) and Sec. V

lane_water.cite: Lane, Leung, Thompson, Cuneo, Water desorption from rapidly heated metal oxide surfaces, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter (doi 10.1088/1361-648X/aae4af)
lane_water.use: water desorption law whose 3000 K cap is analysed here

values.uncertainty: below 5% (Mills Sec. 3.3); 2% below 1000 K, 5% 1000-1700 K for the underlying data (Sec. 3.1)

values.source: mills2004 Eq. (11), analytic integral re-zeroed at 300 K (sealed heat-v2 law)
values.check: within 0.6% of Mills Table 3(a) H(T) rows 400-1600 K (table rounding)

values.source: nippon2020 TP 304 melting range 1399-1454 C (1672.15-1727.15 K, rounded in the sealed law); mills2004 Table 1 Howe liquidus for 304 = 1727 K
values.uncertainty: not stated by the producer; Mills Table 3 assumes 1723 K for 3-series alloys

values.value: latent heat released linearly in T over 1672-1727 K; sensible Cp blended linearly from Cp_solid(1672) to 800
values.uncertainty: the actual solidification path (segregation, delta ferrite) is not represented

values.source: mills2004 Eq. (12) 800 +- 50 J/(kg K), Table 3(b) to 1900 K
values.tag: recommended to 1900 K, model_derived (constant continuation) above
values.uncertainty: +-50 J/(kg K) to 1900 K; above, supported by JANAF constant liquid Cp of the constituents (Kopp-rule value for the nominal composition 796 J/(kg K); Fe 824, Cr 756, Ni 663 J/(kg K))

values.value: Ho & Chu Table 2 rows (PWL), 293 K and 300 K rows interpolated below 300 K
values.uncertainty: 5% below melting, 15% at and above melting

values.tag: recommended slope to 1900 K; model_derived (linear continuation) above
values.uncertainty: not bounded by data above 1900 K (60.99 W/(m K) at 5000 K)

values.source: anchored at hochu1977 1800 K row (extrapolated by source); constant Wiedemann-Franz ratio (same model as ss304-thermal-properties-v2)
values.uncertainty: 15% at 1800 K (Ho & Chu); not bounded above; the anchored ratio equals the Sommerfeld value 2.443e-8 within 0.01%

values.value: solid 7921 - 0.5 (T - 298.2); liquid 6908 - 0.86 (T - 1723) kg/m3; specific-volume blend in the mushy zone
values.tag: recommended (solid to 1672 K, liquid to 1900 K); model_derived above 1900 K and in the mushy zone
values.uncertainty: +-3%; the owner keeps the sealed fixed reference volume with rho_ref = 8000 kg/m3 (1% above Mills at 298 K)

values.source: mills2004 Table 1 typical 304 (19 Cr, 9.3 Ni, 1.0 Mn, 0.5 Si, 0.04 C); Mn, Si, C lumped into Fe
values.uncertainty: grade range 17.5-19.5 Cr, 8-10.5 Ni (1.4301); foil heat composition unknown

values.source: CIAAW standard atomic weights (abridged), as used by ss304-thermal-properties-v2

values.quantity: pure-liquid vapor pressures Fe, Cr, Ni
values.value: ln p = -(dfH_g - dfH_l + (H-H298)_g - (H-H298)_l - T (S_g - S_l))/(R T) at JANAF rows (bar), ln p linear in 1/T between rows
values.tag: recommended up to the liquid-table end (Fe 4000 K, Cr 3500 K, Ni 3600 K); model_derived above (JANAF constant liquid Cp continued)
values.checks: Fe liquid within 1.2% and Ni liquid within 2.4% of alcock1984 over their fit ranges; above the normal boiling point equal to -logKf(liquid) of the same tables within 0.0005 decades

values.value: Raoult a_i = gamma_i x_i, gamma_i = 1, pure-liquid standard state at all T
values.source: mills2004 p. 1667: 'the thermodynamics of the Fe-Cr, Fe-Ni systems are close to ideal'
values.uncertainty: activity coefficients not acquired (open); in the solid alloy the liquid standard state overestimates p by up to x1.8 (Fe), x5.1 (Cr), x2.3 (Ni) between 1000 and 1672 K and by up to x1.4 (Cr) between 1672 K and the element melting points (JANAF logKf of the liquid tables)

values.value: beta_r = 0.18 (net flux = (1 - beta_r) x one-sided HKL flux)
values.uncertainty: valid for strong evaporation into vacuum; must be 0 when the gas owner returns metal atoms explicitly (deposits), to avoid double counting

values.value: eps0_i = m_i h(3000 K) + dHvap_i,JANAF(3000 K)/N_A - 5/2 k 3000 K (Fe 4.254 eV, Cr 4.032 eV, Ni 4.607 eV)
values.uncertainty: implied latent heat (eps0 + 5/2 kT - m h(T)) within 3% of JANAF dHvap over 2000-3500 K, within 5% to 4000 K, up to 10.6% (Cr) at 5000 K; gas electronic excitation (JANAF gas Cp above 5/2 R) is not carried

values.value: 2 k T per atom (one-sided Maxwellian flux) in expected mode; actual packet kinetic energy in quantized mode

values.source: below the published critical-point estimates for steel/304L (sjostrom2023 9500 K; mattsson2004 10000 K; SESAME 4272 about 8000 K)
values.uncertainty: superheated liquid above the 1-bar boiling points (Fe 3133 K, Cr 2952 K, Ni 3157 K, JANAF) is kept as a condensed phase; phase explosion, pressure and hydrodynamics are not modelled
